svg.text: Agentic Customer 360 — Proactive Intervention Desk
Preliminary architecture · mid-term submission · Akshat Agrawal, IIT (BHU) Varanasi
EVENT SOURCES
card_payments
purchase · refund · decline
instant_payments · ach_wire
inbound / outbound transfer
core_banking_ledger
deposit · withdrawal · SI · fee
trading_brokerage
buy · sell · dividend
loan_kyc
kyc · address · dependents
web_app_events
login · search · feature_used
support_logs
ticket · call_transcript
social_signal_consented
life_event_mention
entities.json
profile · accounts · value tier
Expectation checker [T]
daily tick. Compares what
should have arrived against
what did, and injects a
synthetic expectation_breach
INGESTION + TIER-0 REFLEX
deterministic · no LLM in this path · runs on every single event
Normalise & tokenise
schema check · name and account number swapped for
surrogates via a PII vault · merchant → semantic class
Cross-source de-duplication
fingerprint (account, amount, ±5 s) collapses one money
movement reported twice by two different systems
Event-time buffer + watermark
ordered by event_time, never by arrival · allowed
lateness 72 h · a late event revises, it is not dropped
Immutable event log
append-only and replayable · the only source of truth
Incremental feature store [E]
rolling login frequency · balance per account · MCC
histogram · counterparty set · standing-instruction set
· expected-arrival table (amount, period, tolerance)
Cheap detectors [E]
novel category · cadence break · income shortfall · sweep
pair · balance drawdown · SI set-diff · counterparty class
a Signal is emitted only when a test actually fires, so roughly
8% of traffic reaches the expensive tier
Hard-stop scanner [E]
legal threat · self-harm · fraud pattern · sanctions match
Wake controller
decides which specialists run, and over which time window
SWARM — parallel, independent [E]
each agent has its own tools and its own scoped data view
Usage / Engagement
tools: windowed aggregation, cadence model,
trend test
reads: web_app_events slice, feature store, episodic
Transaction / Billing
tools: baseline comparison, counterparty
classifier, drawdown calculator
reads: ledger + payments slice, cohort baselines
Support / Sentiment
tools: sentiment and intent over raw_text,
ticket-history retrieval
reads: support_logs only — no financial scope at all
KYC / Compliance
tools: KYC field diff, sanctions lookup,
deterministic rules engine
reads: loan_kyc, policy index
Life-Event Inference [A]
Does not watch the raw stream at all. It wakes only
when two or more swarm agents have posted
correlated assertions inside the same window.
This is the step that turns three individually
unremarkable signals into one strong one.
DELIBERATION — handoff, then debate only if needed
receives structured assertions, never another agent's reasoning trace
Synthesis / Arbiter [A]
recomputes the posterior over all 14 candidate
states, ranks them, and writes the winning state
into the life-phase slot
handoff package = the assertion set, nothing else
Debate pair [A] — gated
wakes only when the top two hypotheses sit inside
a margin of each other. One agent argues each side.
Resolution is a written rule, not a vibe. If the rule
cannot settle it, confidence is capped and the case
goes to a human on ambiguity alone.
Offer / Eligibility [A]
tools: policy RAG over semantic memory, rules
engine, cost estimator
can reject a candidate action before it is ever drafted
Retention / Action [A]
drafts the intervention. Every factual claim in the
draft must cite event ids pulled from the ledger.
holds a draft tool. It does not hold a send tool.
Critique / Compliance refiner [A]
round-robin passes over the draft: factual grounding,
then tone, then policy. Each pass owns one concern.
Sends the draft back exactly once. A second failure
escalates instead of looping, so a bad draft cannot
burn latency indefinitely.
DECISION GATE + HUMAN DESK
deterministic code, evaluated before any action can exist
Policy matrix
an allow / deny table over
inferred_state × action
checked in code, not asked of a model.
medical_hardship → personalized_offer
is denied outright. No prompt argues past it.
Blast-radius limiter
tools split draft / send. No agent holds a
send or a credit tool. Spend ceiling by
customer value tier; over it, escalation is forced.
Human-in-the-loop desk
a real interrupt. The run parks until a person
approves, rejects or edits the proposal.
The reviewer sees the evidence rows ranked by
how much each moved the posterior, every row
citing its source event ids, and can ask
"why this and not that?" — answered from the
ledger rather than by re-prompting the model.
Approval log
the decision plus the exact evidence snapshot
that was on screen at that moment
Escalation queue
where a hard stop lands, skipping every agent
OUTPUTS
the graded artifact and the evidence it was right
inferred_events.json
as_of_time
inferred_state
confidence_band
action · action_subtype
hitl_status · notes
written daily, again on any band change,
and as a revision when a late event lands
Scoring harness
our output vs a ground_truth.json:
state match · band timing · action match
· lead time against ideal_action_lead_
time_days · red-herring false positives
Trace store
OTel-style spans for every agent run,
tool call, retrieval and handoff, with the
full prompt and response retained
each ledger row links to its span
Metrics
event → decision latency
per-band accuracy
HITL approve / override rate
false positives per red herring
cost per woken deliberation
MEMORY — one shared board per customer, written by agents and read by agents
Working memory
the open case, the window under review,
and what the swarm has concluded so far
on this pass.
cheap to write, discarded once the
situation resolves
Episodic memory (per customer)
past interventions and how they landed,
previous flags, and every HITL approve,
reject or modify decision.
row-level isolation by customer_id, enforced
at the store — not by asking an agent nicely
Evidence Ledger
the shared state board, made append-only. This is the piece the whole design rests on.
One row per assertion, written by exactly one agent:
hypothesis — one of the 14 inferred_state values
direction — supports | opposes
weight — a log-likelihood ratio, not a vote
observed_at (event time) · asserted_at (transaction time)
half_life_days — how fast this piece of evidence stops mattering
source_event_ids — the citation
revoked_by — set when a later event explains the earlier one away
posterior(h, T) = prior(h) + Σᵢ wᵢ · 2^(−Δtᵢ / half_lifeᵢ)
summed over rows where observed_at ≤ T and revoked_by is null — so any past moment can be re-answered exactly
Semantic memory (shared)
offer eligibility rules · compliance policy ·
cohort baselines · merchant → class lexicon
live vector index: upsert on write, tombstone
on supersede, no full rebuild, and a stale
embedding is never allowed to outlive its fact
Access broker
every agent is handed a scoped view object
built from its declared capability set.
An agent without brokerage scope has no
method that can reach brokerage data.
a prompt instruction is not a guardrail
Life-phase slot
the current inferred state, held once and
carried forward with decay applied, so the
Offer agent three weeks later reads the same
conclusion rather than re-deriving its own.
this is what stops a "new parent" inference
from quietly evaporating
Decay and expiry policy
half-lives are set per evidence type, not
globally. A KYC dependents_change barely
decays; one pharmacy purchase is gone in
weeks. An 18-month-old churn flag stops
mattering because its weight has decayed to
nothing, not because a job deleted it.
Why a ledger rather than a state blob
Four requirements in the problem statement turn out to be
the same requirement wearing different hats:
explain the decision → rank the rows by contribution
decay old memory → the half-life term
absorb a late event → append, then recompute for that T
retract a red herring → set revoked_by, recompute
One data structure answers all four. An LLM asked to re-read a
state blob and report its confidence answers none of them
reproducibly, and cannot be audited afterwards.
Cost of this choice: the weights are hand-set from domain reasoning
and tuned on three scenarios. They are not learned. See the report.
synthetic expectation_breach
wake [E]
handoff [A]
hard stop bypasses every agent and lands directly on the human desk
features + raw events
swarm writes assertions
posterior read + life-phase write
HITL outcome → episodic
revision
WHY EACH MECHANISM EXISTS — every row is something I measured in the three practice scenarios, not a hypothetical
What the data actually does
Component that handles it
Why the obvious design gets it wrong
No card spend or app session for 36 days, against a 2-day historical max gap
Expectation checker, daily tick [T]
Nothing is emitted to react to; the only arrivals are salary in and salary out
Salary of $3,800 every 14 days stops, becomes $1,400 of benefits, then nothing
Expected-arrival table + income shortfall detector
Reacting to arrivals can never see a non-arrival
A $12,000 wire and a $12,000 ledger withdrawal, one second apart
Cross-source de-duplication on a fingerprint
Summing naively double-counts the outflow and invents a crisis
$10,000 out of savings and $10,000 into checking, one second apart
Sweep-pair detector — one drawdown, not two movements
Reads as a $10k exfiltration and trips a fraud hold on a sick customer
A $600 electronics purchase, explained the next day as a baby monitor
revoked_by on the ledger row, then recompute and emit a revision
A committed decision with no retraction path simply stays wrong
A ground-truth signal event arrives 48 hours after it happened
Event-time watermark with 72 h allowed lateness
Ordering by arrival time silently drops it from the window it belongs to
Red herrings are the largest amounts; real signals run $85 to $500
Novel-category and counterparty class, not an amount z-score
Ranking by size puts a tuition wire above an ER visit
A new $1,200 daycare instruction appears; rent, gym and utilities stop
Standing-instruction set diff against the historical set
Each individual payment looks perfectly normal on its own
Salary lands at 08:00 and $4,900 of it leaves at 09:15, twice
Cross-source correlation inside a 1-hour window
A deposit and a transfer are both unremarkable in isolation
Roughly 8% of live events carry any signal at all
Tier-0 reflex gates Tier-1; no LLM sees routine traffic
An LLM call per event is 12× the cost and 12× the surface to hallucinate on
Trigger coverage — [E] every ingestion path, the cheap detectors, the hard-stop scanner and the four swarm agents.
[T] the daily expectation tick, the daily checkpoint writer, and periodic KYC re-verification.
[A] life-event correlation, synthesis, the gated debate, offer eligibility, action drafting and the critique refiner.
Coordination patterns — swarm for signal gathering, because the four sources genuinely do not depend on each other.
Handoff into synthesis, scoped to the assertion set. Debate only when the top two hypotheses are close enough to be worth arguing.
Round-robin inside the critique refiner, one concern per pass. Critique-refiner last, because it is the only thing standing before a human.
